variables.claim_asserts: A six-to-sevenfold left/right ventricular dilating-pressure ratio and a matching six-to-sevenfold ventricular wall-thickness ratio.
variables.test_measures: LV/RV free-wall thickness ratios from normal human autopsies and a pressure proxy ratio of NHANES brachial systolic pressure to the midpoint of a published healthy RV systolic range.

modality.note: Autopsy wall measurements directly address thickness; systemic and RV systolic pressures are physiologically relevant proxies for the ventricular pressure ratio.

assumptions.note: The thickness and pressure data come from different populations and RV pressure is a range midpoint rather than paired measurement, but the thickness-only fail condition independently fires in both sexes.

scope.test_scope: Human hearts only: 1,062 morphologically normal UK autopsy hearts, NHANES US adults aged 20-59, and a literature healthy-RV pressure range.

reasons: LV and RV free-wall thickness are the claim's variables; excluding the shared septum and averaging homologous anterior, lateral, and inferior sites is appropriate.
Female R_t = 4.024 and male R_t = 3.936 are below the pre-registered 4.5 refutation boundary, directly contradicting the claimed six-to-sevenfold thickness ratio.

Pressure is less direct: brachial systolic pressure proxies LV peak pressure and 20 mmHg is the midpoint of an unpaired healthy RV range, but the resulting R_p values 5.7 and 6.033 address the claimed proportion.
The interpretation expressly states that human data cover only part of the mammalian scope.
what_would_change_it: Use paired LV and RV pressure measurements together with ventricular free-wall thickness in the same healthy individuals, and include multiple mammalian species to cover the stated scope.
